answer.evidence: `_split_tokens` in radon/raw.py (lines 82-93) is the function that matches the request. It starts with `res = [[]]` and appends a new empty list each time a token matches `(token, value)` on `token_values[:2]`. It then `continue`s, so the separator is never added to any partition. Consecutive separators, or a separator at the start or end, give empty sublists, and nothing filters them out. The only caller, `_logical` at raw.py:173, splits on `(OP, ';')` and sums `aux(sub)` over every partition. That call site therefore needs a review of how empty partitions are handled. I would also check that `aux` copes with an empty `sub_tokens`, because `_find` raises ValueError when the pair is missing. Existing tests in radon/tests/test_raw.py cover `_find` but should get cases for leading, trailing and doubled separators. The complexity.py, metrics.py and visitors.py files work on AST nodes, not token streams, so they do no token splitting. I would spend time there to confirm that no other code partitions tokens or duplicates this logic, and to check how raw-metric results are consumed in metrics.py and visitors.py.

It starts with `res = [[]]` and appends a new empty list each time a token matches `(token, value)` on `token_values[:2]`. It then `continue`s, so the separator is never added to any partition. Existing tests in radon/tests/test_raw.py cover `_find` but should get cases for leading, trailing and doubled separators. The complexity.py, metrics.py and visitors.py files work on AST nodes, not token streams, so they do no token splitting. I would spend time there to confirm that no other code partitions tokens or duplicates this logic, and to check how raw-metric results are consumed in metrics.py and visitors.py.
